notes: The supplied grid-cover proof establishes the dimension bound, the n=0 branch establishes the singleton assertion, and compactness gives finite contents at every positive scale. Review is conditional on the stated N001, without importing its producer or source evidence.

applicability.notes: N001 is instantiated only at A=E in R^n and positive exponents: a>n>0 in S002 and s>0 in S003. Compactness and the routine metric/power facts recorded below have their required conditions. There are no E/M applications.

argument.notes: For n>0 the partition count and Euclidean diameter estimate give cost at most C n^(a/2) h^(a-n). At each fixed positive scale, admissibility holds for all sufficiently small h and the cost tends to zero, so every scale content and hence H^a(E) is zero. N001 and the order argument give D<=n even before finiteness is known. The singleton branch gives D=0. A finite subcover by radius-delta/2 balls gives finite s-cost for arbitrary s,delta>0. All clauses of N002 follow.

dependency_closure.notes: H003 supplies boundedness and finite subcovers; H002 is used in the singleton branch; H001 and the natural domain give exhaustive dimension cases; N001 supplies only its exported measure/dimension implications. F001 precedes the choice of b; C depends on that witness only inside S002. L1-L4 are discharged, F002 is conditional, and F003 is independent of all private witnesses. Arbitrary mesh/exponent and positive s,delta scopes support the claimed universal conclusions.

packet_replay.notes: The implication can be replayed from the four direct premise statements, supplied definitions, earlier F facts and the positively reviewed routine background below. No ancestor proof, source paper, other R body or unexported identification is needed. This judgment concerns mathematical packet sufficiency.

statement_closure.notes: The Euclidean ambient dimension and set are declared; diameter, scale contents, measure, dimension and D have supplied meanings. N001 states the actual positive-exponent conclusions used. N002 explicitly exports extended-real finiteness and bounds, its n=0 clause, and finiteness for every positive s and delta. No local box bound, cover or mesh escapes into the output; D is not used as a real before finiteness is established.

background_notes.fact: A compact subset K of Euclidean R^n is bounded and is contained in [-b,b]^n for some real b>0, also when n=0.

grounds.reason: H003 states that E is compact in the specified Euclidean space.
n is natural and E is a Euclidean subset.

background_notes.justification: The unit balls centered at points of K cover K, hence finitely many suffice by compactness. The triangle inequality bounds the norm of every covered point by 1 plus the maximum norm of the finitely many centers (including 0 in this maximum handles an empty family). Each absolute coordinate is at most the Euclidean norm, so increasing the finite bound to a positive b gives the coordinate box. In R^0 the coordinate conditions are vacuous.

background_notes.fact: For b>0, n>0 and 0<h<=1, the box [-b,b]^n has a finite cover by at most (2b+2)^n h^(-n) coordinate boxes, each of Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies the positive box bound.
S002 chooses b and imposes n>0 and 0<h<=1 before constructing the partition.

background_notes.justification: Put k=ceil(2b/h), a positive integer, and split each interval into k equal closed subintervals of length 2b/k<=h. There are k^n product boxes. The ceiling bound gives k<=2b/h+1<=(2b+1)/h<=(2b+2)/h. For two points in a box each coordinate difference has absolute value at most h, so their squared Euclidean distance is at most n h^2. Thus the asserted diameter bound holds. Calling these boxes cubes does not affect either estimate.

background_notes.fact: For fixed positive finite K and p, K h^p tends to zero as h tends to zero through positive values. For n>0 and a>n, the displayed cover costs C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a equal C n^(a/2)h^(a-n); the associated diameter bound sqrt(n)h also tends to zero.

grounds.reason: Here C=(2b+2)^n is positive finite, n>0, a>n, and h>0; hence p=a-n>0 and K=C n^(a/2)>0 are finite.

background_notes.justification: The positive-real power laws give the cost identity. For any epsilon>0, choosing 0<h<(epsilon/K)^(1/p) gives K h^p<epsilon, by monotonicity and inverse identities for positive powers. For any fixed delta>0, additionally choosing h<=delta/sqrt(n) ensures the diameter bound is at most delta. These choices can also satisfy h<=1. Thus for every fixed delta the nonnegative defining infimum is below every positive epsilon, so it is zero; taking the supremum of these zero contents gives H^a(E)=0. This justifies the limit passage already used in S002 without interchanging an infimum and supremum.

background_notes.fact: For an extended nonnegative number d and finite real t>=0, if d<=a for every finite real a>t, then d<=t and d is finite. In particular, if d<=s for every positive real s, then d=0.

grounds.reason: N001 has yielded D<=a for arbitrary a>n in the n>0 branch; n is finite and nonnegative.

background_notes.justification: The test a=t+1 first excludes d=infinity. If the finite value d were greater than t, the real midpoint (t+d)/2 would contradict the assumed bound. For t=0 combine the resulting upper bound with nonnegativity. Thus no real identification of D is required before proving its finiteness.

background_notes.fact: If K is a compact Euclidean set and s,delta>0, the balls B(x,delta/2), x in K, admit a finite subcover whose members have diameter at most delta and finite total s-cost.

grounds.reason: S004 fixes arbitrary positive real s and delta and selects these balls.
D001 defines diameter as the supremum of distances.
D002 permits finite covers as countable covers and defines scale content as their cost infimum.

background_notes.justification: Each ball is open and contains its center because delta/2>0, so these balls cover K. Compactness supplies finitely many of them. For any two points in a selected ball the triangle inequality gives distance less than delta, so the supremum of distances is at most delta. Each diameter therefore has finite nonnegative s-power, and the finite sum is finite. If an infinite indexing is desired, append empty sets with zero cost. The scale-content infimum is at most this finite sum.
